name: forge-agent
description: Forge: VS Code agent on TrueForge

forge.trueforge.baseUrl.description: Base URL of the local TrueForge server.

forge.models.description: TrueForge model names (provider/model), in order. The first is used; if its provider fails (unreachable, bad key, overloaded, stalled) Forge retries it with backoff and then continues on the next one in a new TrueForge session. Change the first with 'Forge: Switch Model'.

forge.contextBudgetTokens.description: Token budget for automatically injected context.

forge.commandPrefix.description: Shell prefix run before every command the agent runs, e.g. '. .venv/bin/activate &&' so pytest finds your virtual environment. Leave empty to auto-detect: if the workspace has .venv/bin/activate (else venv/bin/activate) Forge uses '. <that>/bin/activate &&'. A value set here always wins; use 'true &&' to run commands with no activation. The effective prefix is shown in the panel's Context section. Windows-style environments (Scripts\activate) are not auto-detected: commands run through a POSIX shell, so set this yourself.

forge.autoAllowCommands.readOnly.markdownDescription: Tier 1. Run these agent commands WITHOUT asking: `git status|diff|log|show|ls-files`, `ls`, `pwd`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep` (no `-r`), `rg`, on workspace paths. They change nothing and run no project code. The whole command must match a strict pattern: no `;`, `&&`, `|`, redirects, `$( )`, backticks, newlines, unknown options, paths outside the workspace, or secrets (`.env*`, `.git`, keys); anything else still shows the Allow card. Auto-allowed commands are marked `auto-allowed (tier 1)` in the panel and logged. Known limit: a symlink inside the workspace that points outside it is not detected.

forge.autoAllowCommands.tests.markdownDescription: Tier 2. Run `pytest` / `python -m pytest`, `ruff check` (never with `--fix`) and `mypy` WITHOUT asking, with the same strict whole-command matching as tier 1 (so `pytest ... 2>&1 | tail` still asks). **Risk: these execute workspace code.** pytest imports and runs your tests and `conftest.py`, including tests the agent just wrote, and mypy loads plugins named in its config; that is the same risk as running them yourself, but it happens without a prompt. Auto-allowed commands are marked `auto-allowed (tier 2)` in the panel and logged.

forge.rollbackOnCancel.description: Roll back edits applied during a run when the run is cancelled.

forge.stallFirstEventSeconds.description: A model that produces no output within this many seconds of the request is treated as stalled (then retried once, then the next model is used). Reasoning models can be silent for a while, so keep this generous. Time spent waiting for your approval or running a tool never counts.

forge.stallIdleSeconds.description: A running model that goes silent for this many seconds between outputs is treated as stalled. Time spent waiting for your approval or running a tool never counts.

forge.resourcePrefix.description: Prefix for the TrueForge resources Forge registers (forge-editor, forge-editor-extras, forge-agent, forge-inline), e.g. 'win2-'. Lets two VS Code windows run side by side against one TrueForge. The environment variable FORGE_RESOURCE_PREFIX wins. Reload the window after changing it.
